window_overflow_before_measurement.why_this_is_here: This is an unplanned but clean 'before' reading for the separate three-star bug about game notes being thrown away. It was taken on the maintainer's own settings - character voice on, thinking at medium - which is the only shape that shows the problem.
window_overflow_before_measurement.speed_questions: none of the three warned. The reply budget in Speed is 1312 and the prompts ran about 1050 to 1525 tokens, comfortably inside the window.
window_overflow_before_measurement.measured: All three Strategy questions tripped the over-the-window warning, by 703 to 780 tokens. All three Speed questions did not.
window_overflow_before_measurement.inference_not_yet_proven: Ollama reported reading about 2,080 to 2,120 tokens of prompt, where the plugin estimated about 2,690 to 2,760. The window minus the reply budget is 1,984. The numbers landing just above that line is what truncation would look like, so the start of the prompt was most likely cut. This is a strong reading, not a proof - nothing in the log states outright what was dropped.
window_overflow_before_measurement.worth_noting: The answers were still good - one named the Glyphid Dreadnought and its armour plates, one named Hollow Bough. Either the surviving end of the prompt carried enough, or the model already knew this game. That is exactly why this bug went unnoticed: a dropped note does not always produce an obviously bad answer.
window_overflow_before_measurement.what_this_gives_the_next_step: 3 of 3 Strategy questions overflowing is the before number for the device check that closes the notes-thrown-away bug. After the prompt slimming and the reply-shortening change land, the same run must warn on zero.
